findings.title: Service shutdown does not close or await the active effective-defaults probe
findings.description: defaults() creates a separate NativeRpc in a local variable. RuntimeService.close() only closes this.native, so it can return while an already-running defaults probe is still waiting for initialize/thread/start. The main shutdown path then exits the worker without waiting for that probe. Linux systemd cgroup cleanup may mitigate process leakage in production, but the runtime close contract and supported Windows development shutdown do not verify that independently spawned process tree. A close/config-read race can also continue the defaults path after the service is closed.
reproduction: Compile the unchanged source with node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --outDir .work/r1-runtime-build.
Run node .work/r1-runtime-lifecycle.mjs. It supplies a main FakeNative config/read response and starts a separate local Node protocol child which answers initialize but holds thread/start.
Wait until the child writes its PID, call await service.close(), then probe that PID with process.kill(pid, 0).
findings.cleanup: The reproduction explicitly called close on the captured probe after observation; its pending request rejected runtime_lost/unknown and the Node process exited normally.
findings.recommendation: Track the dedicated probe as service-owned state, fence probe creation against shutdown, and have close cancel and await both the primary RPC and any in-flight probe before claiming cleanup.

findings.title: A delayed terminal-open request can create a terminal after its gateway disconnect cleanup
findings.description: gatewayDisconnected/clientDisconnected clean only the terminals currently present. An authenticated /rpc body which was already in flight can finish after the final event WebSocket has closed and the cleanup snapshot has completed. There is no gateway/client disconnect generation bound to that HTTP request and no event-channel admission check before terminal creation, so the late terminal/open starts command/exec with both timeout and output cap disabled and has no remaining disconnect event to terminate it. WorkerClient uses separate HTTP requests and does not abort them when its event WebSocket closes.
reproduction: Run node .work/r1-runtime-late-terminal.mjs against the compiled current modules.
Open an authenticated worker /events WebSocket, start a terminal/open HTTP request with its declared Content-Length, and send only the first 20 bytes.
Terminate the final event WebSocket and wait for gatewayDisconnected() to finish, then send the rest of the original HTTP request body.
Inspect the HTTP result, service terminal count, and FakeNative command history.
findings.cleanup: The probe used FakeNative and never spawned a shell; it closed the worker HTTP server, event socket, and service afterward.
findings.recommendation: Bind terminal admissions to a connection generation which cannot be reopened by requests admitted before disconnect; revoke that generation before cleanup and check it at the final native write. Ensure late HTTP work cannot create ownerless terminals when the gateway event channel has disappeared.

findings.title: Management completion publishes maintenance=true but never publishes its release
findings.description: A management mutation emits its receipt and status while #maintenance is still true, then clears #maintenance in finally without emitting another state. Browsers have already set activityReady=false. Custom-provider model discovery returns source=provider and ModelCatalog does not trigger onApplied/reload in that branch, so an otherwise idle runtime emits no later state to restore the UI; management failures have the same problem. The server internally permits work again while the browser keeps new-task submission disabled.
reproduction: Start with connected=true, activity.unknown=false and no active work.
Invoke system/models/refresh against a provider discovery manager substitute, with a fresh operation ID and a manager result that does not restart the worker.
Record Dispatcher state events and compare its current status after the call resolves.
The final published status has maintenance=true, whereas dispatcher.status().maintenance is false; feeding the published event to useEvents leaves activityReady=false.
findings.observed: Bounded in-memory source probe reproduced lastBroadcast.maintenance=true, actualStatus.maintenance=false and browserActivityReady=false. The probe's result projection used source=native; provider result differences do not alter Dispatcher state ordering, and the production provider UI branch was separately traced to ensure it does not mask the missing broadcast.
findings.recommendation: Publish a current state after releasing the maintenance flag in finally, including the failure path, and add a focused lifecycle assertion on the last externally emitted state.

findings.title: Same-worker event reconnection does not resynchronize history or pending prompts
findings.description: When only the gateway-to-worker event WebSocket drops, the browser WebSocket stays open. RuntimeService keeps its epoch and the worker reconnect snapshot contains status only, with no missed notification/prompt replay. useEvents restores runtimeConnected/activityReady but does not change revision; App's resourceEpoch therefore remains identical. Conversation history, resume/default state and prompt/list are not refreshed. A completion or approval created during the event gap can be absent indefinitely even though the UI reports a healthy connection, leaving incomplete history or an invisible pending decision.
reproduction: Keep an authenticated browser WebSocket open with runtime epoch E and a loaded conversation.
Drop only the gateway-to-worker event channel; let the native worker continue and produce a turn completion or a new approval during the gap.
Reconnect to the same RuntimeService; its initial state snapshot still has epoch E.
No browser onopen occurs, no hook revision advances and no history/prompt/resume generation changes; missed events are not recovered.
findings.observed: Current source lifecycle confirms same epoch and no replay. A source-transformed useEvents probe fed connected=true(E), connected=false, connected=true(E): epoch and revision stayed E/1 before and after while runtimeConnected and activityReady returned true.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a resynchronization generation when the upstream runtime/event connection recovers even with the same process epoch, and use it to re-read pending prompts, thread metadata/history, resume state and other connection-sensitive resources before declaring readiness.

findings.title: Expired or restarted gateway sessions cannot return the open page to login
findings.description: SessionApp checks authentication only on its initial mount and sets authenticated=false only after a successful logout. A 12-hour session expiration, logout from another document or gateway restart invalidates the in-memory session, but subsequent 401 RPCs merely become local errors and the event socket retries indefinitely. The existing logout control also requires a valid session; its 401 rejects before setAuthenticated(false), so it cannot reopen Login. Users must discover that a manual page reload is required, including after the product's own restart flow.
reproduction: Open a logged-in workspace and retain an unsent draft.
Expire/remove the server session (or restart the gateway).
Observe RPC unauthorized responses and failed WebSocket reconnections.
Try the workspace logout button: DELETE /api/session returns 401, Api.logout rejects, authenticated remains true and no Login screen appears.
findings.observed: Deterministic code-path audit across auth expiration, authenticated DELETE, Api error handling, useEvents close handling and SessionApp state ownership. No real browser/session-expiry integration was executed.
findings.recommendation: Handle authoritative authentication loss centrally or recheck the session after connection recovery failure, return the document to a clear login state, and preserve drafts and operation recovery metadata.

findings.title: Archive action follows the sidebar filter instead of the selected conversation
findings.description: The archived state is the thread-list filter, but the current conversation menu also uses it to choose both the label and thread/archive versus thread/unarchive. Toggling the sidebar filter does not navigate away or change the selected thread's actual archive state. Thus an ordinary conversation immediately offers Restore and sends unarchive after the filter is changed to archived; an archived conversation opened from that list offers Archive again after the filter is changed back. Deep links also begin with the default false filter regardless of the target's archive state.
reproduction: Open an ordinary unarchived conversation.
Toggle the sidebar's archived-list filter without selecting another conversation.
Open conversation actions: the same conversation now shows Restore and sends thread/unarchive.
Alternatively open an archived conversation, switch the sidebar to normal history, and observe Archive/thread/archive on the still-selected archived conversation.
findings.observed: Direct state/action trace: onArchived only toggles archived, while the current menu derives its action and label from that exact filter variable. No browser interaction is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Track or query the selected thread's archive state independently of list filtering, and derive the menu action from the selected resource's state.

findings.title: Provider and HTTPS writes bypass an unfinished management transaction
findings.description: activate and restart enforce require_recovered_transactions, but provider_change (including confirmed catalog application) does not. setup_https only rejects pending HTTPS transactions. After an interrupted release/provider/HTTPS selection, these entrypoints can create and commit a second transaction and restart services on the uncommitted configuration. If the second write is also interrupted, repair rejects the multiple pending records and cannot automatically recover.

reproduction.platform: Windows local Python filesystem fixture; System and ProviderStore side effects substituted, actual validation/dispatch/receipt/transaction writes executed
reproduction.setup: Create a persisted release transaction with phase selected and an old healthy release, then call Manager.dispatch(provider/write) with a valid expected provider revision and fresh UUID.

findings.recommendation: Apply the common unfinished-transaction guard before preparing or dispatching provider/catalog and HTTPS writes; keep read-only discovery/status and explicit recovery available.

findings.title: HTTPS test fixtures make the mandatory source-security scan fail
findings.description: The two opaque private-key fixtures embed literal PEM private-key headers. The unchanged scanner intentionally detects these markers in every source file, so the first source-security step in affected.yml exits nonzero for this snapshot before type/build/tests can run. These are fake fixture contents, not evidence of an actual leaked private key.

reproduction.note: The scanner also emitted two private-home findings in existing evidence outside this assigned source inventory; those evidence conclusions were not opened or reviewed and are not used as a separate finding.

findings.recommendation: Construct safe fixture marker bytes at runtime as the tooling tests already do, retaining the scanner rules and then rerun the source gate.

findings.title: Git-object scanning loses parent paths and misses prohibited nested runtime trees
findings.description: History mode applies pathFindings only to each tree entry basename. Rules for reference/runtime and reference/evidence require the parent path, so a Git tree containing those generated directories is reported clean when no blob independently matches a secret regex. The source scan detects these same relative paths, leaving the history scan inconsistent with its declared artifact coverage.

reproduction.fixture: Fresh Git repository under ignored .work; add only reference/runtime/fixture.txt and run git write-tree, without reading any existing Git history.

findings.recommendation: Reconstruct and scan repository-relative paths when traversing tree objects, while retaining dangling-object scanning and content-redacted diagnostics.

findings.title: A failed install collision leaves state that can stop or delete a pre-existing service unit
findings.description: initialize checks service-unit collisions only after creating instance state, installation metadata, sudo policy, control code and possibly the worker unit. A pre-existing gateway unit therefore causes a late collision but leaves a Manager-loadable partial instance. activate can stop/start/enable the existing unit without verifying ownership. More directly, uninstall blindly stops and unlinks both fixed unit names, deleting the pre-existing unit even though installation refused to claim it.

reproduction.platform: Relocated Windows filesystem; OS identities, privilege validation and system commands substituted. Real initialization files and uninstall unlinks executed.
reproduction.note: An initial combined uninstall probe reached a Windows read-only sudo-file PermissionError after unit deletion; the isolated ownership probe removed that incidental platform condition and returned successfully.

findings.independentCrossCheck: A separate read-only subagent confirmed both activation and the direct uninstall deletion path.
findings.recommendation: Preflight all unit/sudo/drop-in collisions before initialization writes, persist explicit ownership or initialization-completion facts, and require that ownership before resume or uninstall manages service units.

findings.title: HTTPS recovery cannot restore a gateway that was running with its worker stopped
findings.description: prior_service_state accepts gateway active with worker stopped. recover_https_transaction starts the recorded gateway, whose generated Wants=worker dependency starts the worker as well. confirm_service_state then rejects the newly running worker, leaves the transaction recovering, and repair repeats the same failure. The control updater already uses per-role startup barriers for this legitimate service-state combination; HTTPS recovery has no equivalent.

reproduction.platform: Local files with substituted systemd; start explicitly models the Wants relation read from real render_units output. This is not actual Linux systemd execution.
reproduction.fault: One-time daemon reload failure during HTTPS setup

observed.message: Previously stopped HTTPS service is running

findings.independentCrossCheck: A separate read-only subagent confirmed worker stop does not stop gateway because the unit uses Wants rather than BindsTo/Requires, and repair re-enters the same recovery function.
findings.recommendation: Use stop-confirmed per-role start barriers or an equivalent dependency-safe restoration mechanism so recovery preserves the original active set.

findings.title: Conversation creation suppresses the owner check before its first turn
findings.reproduction: The independent ignored test holds thread/read after thread/start returns a fresh thread, revokes the browser owner, calls clientDisconnected, and releases the read. The real RuntimeService still writes turn/start and returns an inProgress turn. Recorded native writes are thread/start, thread/read, turn/start; the supplied owner-check hook is invoked once only.
findings.cause: compositeContext wraps beforeWrite with boundaryNotified, but the HTTP worker supplies requireOwner at src/runtime/main.ts:67-69. Its authorization must be checked at every native mutation. A fresh thread bypasses history admission, so deleting history traversals on disconnection does not compensate for the skipped hook.
findings.impact: Closing a browser owner or its gateway event connection after creation can still start model work and tool execution after that owner has been revoked.
findings.expected: Check current owner/channel authority immediately before both native writes. Keep any one-time durable dispatch bookkeeping distinct from the repeated owner check. If thread creation already succeeded and the first turn is then rejected, preserve conversation_start_incomplete with unknown overall delivery and phase/threadId/cause metadata; do not replay creation or the first turn automatically.

findings.title: Valid maximum-size attachments overflow the Base64 regular expression stack
findings.reproduction: On Node v24.15.0, call the real Attachments.upload with Buffer.alloc(4*1024*1024,97).toString("base64"), a normal filename and text/plain MIME type. The 5,592,408-byte canonical Base64 string is below the 6 MiB text limit and encodes exactly the allowed 4 MiB. The grouped repetition in the regular expression throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The independent test asserts this actual failure; a 1 MiB control succeeds in the direct regex probe.
findings.cause: The repeating grouped Base64 validator uses the JavaScript RegExp stack proportional to sufficiently large valid input before binary quota validation or storage writes.
findings.impact: Files permitted by the advertised 4 MiB limit cannot be uploaded. The untyped RangeError is converted by the worker to internal_error with unknown delivery even though no attachment was written, leaving misleading recovery state.
findings.expected: Validate Base64 with a bounded-stack implementation and preserve malformed-input/size rejection before any mutation. Exercise a canonical file at the declared limit, padding variants, and invalid input without reducing the documented limit merely to conceal the failure.

findings.title: Transient request capacity permanently abandons disconnected terminal cleanup
findings.reproduction: An independent stdio substitute runs behind the real NativeRpc and RuntimeService. Open the allowed 16 terminals under eight owners and one event channel, then submit 48 short hold requests so the native pending map reaches its permitted 64 slots. Call gatewayDisconnected for that channel. Every command/exec/terminate is rejected locally as capacity/not_sent and swallowed. After all 48 holds resolve after 200 ms, native.connected remains true, pending remains 16, and runtime activity still reports 16 terminals. There is no retained cleanup retry. The test finally closes the native subprocess.
findings.cause: clientDisconnected catches every terminate error as though it proved a lost native connection. Capacity rejection and definitive native errors leave the connection alive. gatewayDisconnected awaits this falsely successful cleanup once and has no follow-up path.
findings.impact: A routine gateway reconnect under permitted load can leave shells running with no connected owner and no future termination attempt. These processes and terminal slots can remain indefinitely after temporary congestion has cleared, and they block subsequent maintenance.
findings.expected: Track cleanup obligations until a terminal exit or whole-process cleanup is positively confirmed. Retry safely after not_sent capacity errors, or fail the epoch and confirm process-tree cleanup. A rejected terminate is not an acknowledgement that the process is gone.

findings.title: Late attachment removal overwrites the departed draft and blanks the current composer
findings.reproduction: Store draft A with unsent text and an attachment, plus draft B with different unsent text. Start removing the attachment from A while attachment/remove is deferred. Navigate to B without unmounting the shared Composer/useDraft. Resolve removal successfully. The stale removal callback uses the current attachmentRef but the previous onAttachmentsChange closure. useDraft.ts lines 12-14 now sees a different current key and starts from emptyDraft(A), persists A with empty text, and replaces the displayed draft state with key A. The B composer immediately becomes blank while its stored B text is still present. Confirmed by the first test in .work/r2-control-web/edge.test.tsx.
findings.impact: A successful ordinary attachment deletion can irreversibly erase unsent text in the original draft and make the newly selected draft disappear from the visible input. Preserve the original draft contents while removing the deleted ID from that original draft, and prevent late completion from publishing into the currently selected draft.

evidence.result: Two tests passed before the later HTTP fixture was added; test one asserts the observed wrong A text and blank current textarea.

findings.title: History merge permanently displays a streamed answer before the user message that preceded it
findings.reproduction: Open or reconnect to an active conversation and defer the history response. First deliver item/agentMessage/delta for answer item A, creating the current turn with only A and marking it touched. Then deliver history for the same turn containing chronological items [user question Q, answer A]. mergeHistory initializes its Map from current [A], then appends Q from history, producing [A,Q]. item/completed later replaces A at its existing index and leaves [A,Q]. The touched check also discards any historical answer prefix, so only the newly received suffix is visible before completion. Confirmed by the second test in .work/r2-control-web/edge.test.tsx.
findings.impact: Routine navigation or reconnection while a turn is streaming reverses question/answer display order for the remainder of the visit, and loses already-generated answer text until a complete item arrives. Merge authoritative historical order with current live content instead of using arrival order as item chronology.

evidence.result: Two deterministic tests passed, asserting incorrect order answer,question both before and after a full item/completed notification.

findings.title: HTTP lease admission reports a known accepted operation as not_sent before receipt replay
findings.reproduction: Through a short loopback GatewayServer fixture with an in-memory Ledger and explicit worker substitute, authenticate and open the browser event connection. Submit turn/start with operation ID X and receive an accepted durable receipt. Close the browser event connection and wait for server-side lease cleanup. Resubmit exactly the same method, params and ID X using the still-valid authenticated cookie and CSRF token. The response is connection_required with delivery:not_sent, although Ledger.read(X).state is accepted and worker write count remains one. server.ts rejects before Dispatcher.call reaches reserve/replay. Confirmed by .work/r2-control-web/receipt-http.test.ts.
findings.impact: The public RPC endpoint gives a conflicting delivery fact for an already accepted identity whenever its connection lease is gone. A client retry can receive apparent not-sent evidence instead of the durable accepted result. Existing receipt/fingerprint checks must precede admission that is only required for new dispatch, while retaining different-payload conflict rejection.

evidence.result: One test passed after correcting the fixture to wait for server-side disconnect cleanup. The first fixture run raced client-side close and was not counted as bug evidence.

findings.title: Run root-owned deployment fixtures under a supported CI identity
findings.reproduction: The affected job uses the ordinary ubuntu-24.04 runner and invokes node scripts/select-tests.mjs --base "$CHANGE_BASE" --head "$CHANGE_HEAD" --run deploy without privilege elevation. Any deploy implementation change selects all tests/deploy/test_*.py. tests/deploy/test_control_update.py:87-115 creates files as the current user and substitutes only ancestry/process/snapshot behavior; update still calls deploy/control_update.py:47-55 -> inspect_tree(root_owned=True), which requires st_uid == 0 at deploy/safe_fs.py:195-197. Its unguarded tests therefore fail for a non-root runner. tests/deploy/test_management_boundaries.py similarly feeds runner-owned files into require_owned. Even after those failures are addressed, tests/deploy/test_https.py:73 and tests/deploy/test_install_recovery.py:246 explicitly skip their root-ownership fixtures for that user, and scripts/select-tests.mjs:133-136 correctly returns nonzero for skips. Reproduce on the configured non-root Ubuntu runner with node scripts/select-tests.mjs --changed deploy/control_update.py --run deploy. This finding is established by the complete source execution path; a real Linux runner was not executed during this audit.
findings.impact: Deployment changes cannot obtain a passing affected CI result in the configured job. The fix must provide truthful execution of root-ownership fixtures while preserving ordinary unprivileged checks; silently skipping them or weakening the ownership checks would conceal the coverage gap.

findings.title: Reject SQLite rollback journal artifacts in source and Git scans
findings.reproduction: Create a new isolated Git repository containing a tracked gateway.sqlite-journal file, then call auditSource and auditGitObjects from release-audit.mjs. Both return status clean with zero artifacts. The generated-artifact suffix only accepts .sqlite/.sqlite3 plus -wal/-shm, omitting the -journal sidecar already recognized by deploy/journal.py:18. Executed reproducer: .work/r2-deploy-scanner-probe.mjs; results: .work/r2-deploy-scanner-results.json. The source probe scanned the complete 33-byte harmless sidecar fixture; Git mode scanned its blob and tree, also clean.
findings.impact: A force-tracked or historical SQLite rollback journal can pass both release checks and enter the audited source snapshot even though generated database state must remain outside Git. Such journals can retain prior database page contents. Add the rollback-journal suffix to the shared path policy and cover source plus historical trees.

findings.title: Recognize supported credential patterns in UTF-16 text
findings.reproduction: Create settings.txt as BOM-prefixed UTF-16LE containing an api_key assignment whose value is a synthetic sk- token followed by 32 alphabetic fixture characters. Track it in a new isolated Git repository. auditSource reads all 94 bytes and returns clean; auditGitObjects scans the complete blob/tree and also returns clean. scanStream decodes each byte with latin1, leaving NUL characters between every credential character, so both the api-token and literal-secret rules miss the same token that they detect in ordinary ASCII/UTF-8. Executed reproducer and results are .work/r2-deploy-scanner-probe.mjs and .work/r2-deploy-scanner-results.json. No real credentials were used or emitted.
findings.impact: A normal UTF-16 configuration or text file can contain a credential matching an explicitly supported rule while both release scan modes certify it clean. Decode recognized UTF-16 encodings with chunk-safe handling, or classify unsupported encoded text as incomplete rather than clean, and add source/blob regressions.

findings.title: Reject a failed Windows tree kill even when the native root has exited
findings.description: The taskkill callback resolves on `code === 0 || this.exited`. If the native root exits after stop() starts taskkill but before taskkill enumerates the tree, taskkill returns 128 and the child close event sets this.exited. The OR condition then reports successful process-tree cleanup despite live descendants. The earlier already-exited guard does not cover this race.
findings.impact: On Windows development/isolated-probe runs, a terminal command or other native descendant can survive a supposedly successful NativeRpc.close(). Defaults probing can cache and return a result after a false cleanup acknowledgement, and service shutdown can report cleanup success while orphaned work remains. Production Linux launcher cleanup is a separate branch and is not implicated by this reproduction.

steps: Compile the frozen source with `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --outDir .work/r3-runtime-probe-dist` and copy package.json into that ignored output root for runtime metadata.

Run `node .work/r3-runtime-exit-probe.mjs` on Windows. Its local stdio fixture completes initialization, spawns a detached idle Node descendant, sends a valid request result, then exits ten milliseconds later. The caller immediately awaits NativeRpc.close() with dev:true.
The probe observes the actual taskkill exit code through a pass-through spawn wrapper and checks descendant liveness after close() settles. It does not mock taskkill, timing or process termination.

All three runs recorded taskkillExitCode:128, cleanup:resolved and descendantAlive:true. The probe finally explicitly taskkills every fixture descendant; a separate follow-up liveness check confirmed all three were gone.

findings.recommendation: Treat nonzero taskkill exit as an unconfirmed cleanup failure even if the root has closed. Add a focused regression for root exit during tree-kill startup; only acknowledge successful cleanup with evidence for the process tree.

findings.title: Recover or close a terminal whose accepted HTTP result is lost
findings.description: When terminal/open is durably accepted and its receipt is received over the still-live WebSocket, losing only its HTTP response leaves the TerminalPanel without terminalId. Receipt reconciliation retains accepted status but discards result.terminalId. The recovery row then offers only acknowledgement, while the panel offers another open with no recover or close action. Later output for the accepted terminal is ignored. The existing runtime keeps this shell running without a timeout until its authenticated owner disconnects; it occupies a terminal slot and prevents configuration changes while it exists. This concerns a positively accepted result, not the unavoidable uncertainty of a request without a receipt.
findings.reproduction: Open a terminal with a stable owner; deliver its accepted receipt containing terminalId before rejecting the fetch with a transport error. The isolated component probe observes one accepted operation, an enabled open button, no close button, no query-receipt button, and zero terminal/close requests. Owned output afterward still does not restore controls.

findings.recommendation: Keep or reread the durable terminal result and bind an explicit recover/close action to its original live owner, or safely close the accepted orphan when recovery is possible; do not silently discard its resource identity.

findings.title: Retain a bounded HTTP output reservation until the response drains or closes
findings.description: GatewayServer releases the only request reservation immediately after json calls res.end, although a slow client can leave that response buffered. The byte budget charges request input only, the sockets limit applies to WebSockets only, and there is no global HTTP output/connection budget or response write timeout. Node applies per-connection pipeline backpressure but additional authenticated HTTP connections remain admitted, so unread response data can accumulate outside the declared budgets.
findings.reproduction: A real isolated gateway with one authenticated event owner and eight paused HTTP readers accepted three sequential thread/read requests on each connection. Each response was 6 MiB, within the runtime history and gateway response limits. All 24 requests were forwarded; eight responses remained not writableFinished with combined writableLength 50337032 bytes. A separate bounded probe admitted 52 independent HTTP connections using the same owner, confirming the WebSocket count does not cap HTTP connections. Initial single-response probes were absorbed by OS send buffers and were not counted as proof of JavaScript response retention.
evidence: .work/r3-control-web-slow-http.test.ts
.work/r3-control-web-http-result.json
src/runtime/types.ts:9
findings.recommendation: Charge encoded responses against a global output budget before retention and release only on finish/close, with bounded active HTTP connections and a slow-response timeout or equivalent explicit admission policy.

findings.title: Bound management request staging before creating privileged files or units
findings.trigger: A gateway-identity caller invokes its permitted manage rpc entry with a recognized mutation while systemd launch/wait fails, times out or the caller disconnects. Each invocation uses a new request UUID before the envelope, operationId, recovery gate or receipt-retention budget is checked.
findings.impact: Failed or interrupted calls retain root-owned request JSON under state/requests, including raw provider input. No count/aggregate-byte quota or stopped-unit reclamation applies to these request/result objects. The existing 10000-receipt cap does not cover them, so even invalid requests or replays can grow privileged state storage without bound and exhaust the filesystem. Successful restart transactions also outlive the gateway caller, leaving result files that the killed waiter cannot consume.
findings.evidence: The ignored probe prefilled the 10000 receipt count, then made three helper_main RPC calls with method provider/write, no operationId and an extra 65536-character field. Only require_linux/Layout/stdio and the OS command boundary were substituted; production request serialization, UUID allocation, staging and exception handling ran against a fresh isolated directory. Simulated systemd launch failure retained 1/2/3 files totaling 65612/131224/196836 bytes; each call still attempted one systemd launch and created zero new receipts. The retained fixture request input remained readable from each staged file. No root/systemd command was executed.
reproduction: Use an isolated temporary Layout and create state/requests and state/receipts.
Populate state/receipts with 10000 ordinary fixture records to reach the existing receipt count limit.

Invoke cli.helper_main with argv [manage,rpc] and a provider/write JSON body lacking operationId and containing a 64 KiB extra field; substitute the systemd command function with a command_failed exception.
Repeat three times and observe state/requests grows by a fresh input file each time although the requests are invalid and the receipt budget is already full.
findings.recommendation: Validate the bounded mutation envelope before staging and enforce a root-owned aggregate count/byte/in-flight budget under a separate short admission lock before creating a request or transient unit. Retain uncertain outcomes safely, but refuse further admission at the bound; reclaim request/result files only after confirming the owning unit has stopped and the durable receipt preserves the needed recovery facts. Add focused coverage for launch failure, waiter disconnect, invalid request flooding and receipt replay.

findings.title: Correct the resource-policy description of thread/resume as a read
findings.trigger: A reader follows the History resource-policy paragraph to implement or review a resume request.
findings.impact: The paragraph calls thread/resume a read-classified recovery read, contradicting the explicit mutation semantics documented at line 20 and implemented by the write/continue method classification. Resume may consume persisted native work, so this stale text misstates its operation and receipt requirements. This is documentation-only; the inspected implementation keeps the write boundary and does not expose a read-route authorization bypass.

findings.impact: The operation reports a committed legacy transition while preserving a provider explicitly unsupported in legacy mode. The published worker unit removes the instance requirements bind and the separate host configuration check, and its config-check unit is deleted. findings.title: Bound tar extension metadata before the privileged parser reads it
findings.body: extract_tar opens and iterates tarfile before its member budgets run. Python tarfile eagerly reads a complete PAX extended header into one buffer and hides that header from the yielded members, so MAX_FILES, MAX_FILE and MAX_BYTES do not constrain it. A source archive containing one tiny allowed file and a large compressed PAX record can therefore exhaust the privileged installer memory before Builder.prepare reaches its bounded offline build stages. This affects the shared extraction entry point; pinned upstream downloads are integrity-checked, while operator-supplied application archives are parsed here before application-input validation. Enforce extension-header and aggregate decompressed-input limits before tarfile consumes the metadata, preserving required official archive compatibility.
findings.trigger: Install or update with an application source tar archive containing oversized PAX extension metadata.
findings.impact: Privileged installer CPU/memory denial of service outside the advertised candidate resource bounds. Actual OOM was not attempted.

findings.title: Fence prior realtime sessions before assigning thread-only notifications to a new owner

A delayed closed event also closes B and releases its activity barrier while B may still be running. findings.title: Enforce the lockfile byte limit before reading it into root memory
findings.trigger: An administrator installs or updates from a candidate source archive containing an oversized pnpm-lock.yaml. The source archive permits a regular member up to 512 MiB; dependency_input is called by Builder.prepare before entering the bounded isolated fetch/build units.
findings.impact: Path.read_text reads the complete candidate lock and lock.encode creates another full-size allocation before the 8 MiB check rejects it. A permitted 512 MiB archive member can therefore cause approximately 1 GiB of root-process allocation before rejection. The direct root install/update preparation path has no memory cgroup bound here, so a malformed candidate can create host memory pressure or OOM disruption while the existing deployment is still running.
evidence: deploy/build.py:116 reads the complete file; line 117 evaluates len(lock.encode()) before rejecting sizes above 8 MiB.
deploy/safe_fs.py:19 permits 512 MiB per extracted file; deploy/build.py:232-235 extracts and calls dependency_input before isolated stages.
deploy/cli.py:163-170 and 195-199 invoke install/update preparation directly as root; the 512 MiB transient manager unit applies to RPC operations, not this source-build path.
findings.recommendation: Read at most 8 MiB + 1 byte from the root-owned candidate file in binary mode, reject overflow before decoding or copying, and add an oversized-lock regression that checks bounded reading rather than only the final exception.

findings.title: An expired pairing status query leaves the next pairing check disabled until the settings owner remounts
findings.evidence: The status handler sets the component-wide checking boolean true. Its finally clears checking only while scopeRef.current still matches the original pairScope. Expiry clears pairingId at line 50, changing the scope. A late status completion therefore cannot clear checking. Neither the owner-reset effect at line 48 nor creating a new pairing at line 62 resets or replaces that pending state. The next pairing renders its check button disabled by the retained checking=true at line 63.
reproduction: Render RemoteSettings with a stable epoch and connectionId; create pair-1 with an imminent expiry. Start its pairing/status read and hold the mocked response pending.
Allow pair-1 to expire, so the expiry message appears and pairingId is cleared.
Variant A: resolve the old read with claimed=false, then explicitly confirm and create pair-2. Variant B: create pair-2 first, then resolve the old read with claimed=true.
In both variants code-2 is visible but Check whether paired remains disabled. Clicking it dispatches no second pairing/status request.
Change connectionId to a new owner. The prior code is removed; explicitly creating code-3 produces an enabled check button. Its current claimed=true response hides code-3 normally.
findings.actual: Both bounded probes reproduced newStatusDisabled=true with pairingStarts=2 and statusReads=1. The late claimed=true response did not hide the new code, so the existing data-scope guard works, but its busy state is stranded. A new connection owner restored querying; a current successful claim still hid its code.
findings.expected: After expiry and explicit creation of a new pairing, its own check must be available and have independently owned pending state. A late old response must neither disable the new check nor clear a newer pending check nor apply the old claimed result.
findings.impact: The current mounted settings owner cannot query the new pairing status through this control; the user must remount the owner, for example by reopening settings or establishing a new connection. This is a functional UX dead end. The probes did not show an authorization bypass or stale claimed data applied to the new pairing.
findings.recommendation: Bind pending status-query state and cancellation to the current pairing owner/generation, and clear only the request that owns that state. Add focused regression coverage for expiry and replacement while an old status query is pending, including late success/failure, new-query overlap, disconnect/reconnect, and environment change.

findings.title: MCP tool images bypass decoded-media budgets and load automatically
findings.description: McpContent trusts a declared image MIME type, a permissive Base64 character regex and a 1,400,000-character bound, then immediately emits an img with a data URL for every image entry. It never applies mediaBytes/mediaMime, reads image dimensions, limits total preview pixels or requires a separate preview action. McpPanel renders retained tool content immediately. A connected tool can therefore return a compact, schema-valid image that fits all serialized-byte caps but exceeds the existing 40,000,000-pixel policy and drives excessive browser decode memory/CPU. Multiple images also receive src simultaneously. This can freeze or terminate the active browser tab and disrupt unsaved work. The audit demonstrated missing guards and size feasibility; it did not decode a large image or reproduce an actual OOM.

evidence.observation: Only MIME/encoded-string checks precede automatic img creation; map has no preview count or pixel budget.
Accepted tool result is read into the attempt and its content is rendered through McpContent without an explicit image-preview control.
Body retention is capped at 2 MiB of UTF-8 JSON, which does not bound image dimensions or decoded memory.
Native MCP result validation checks the protocol schema and serialized historyBytes cap (8 MiB); it has no image-header/pixel validation.
Tool content is Array<JsonValue>; the official result contract does not supply a decoded-media budget.
Existing shared helpers enforce Base64/byte validity, PNG/GIF/WebP/JPEG signatures/dimensions, dimensions <=16,384 per side, positive dimensions and <=40,000,000 pixels; MCP does not call them.
Other message media requires an explicit load/preview action before assigning an image src.

reproduction: Load the current McpContent and mediaMime modules with Vite SSR and render McpContent with React renderToStaticMarkup only; no browser or raster decoder is involved.

Supply a 24-byte synthetic PNG header with IHDR width=12000 and height=12000. McpContent emits one img with data:image/png;base64 src. mediaMime rejects the same 144,000,000-pixel header. The tool-body JSON is 95 UTF-8 bytes.
Supply 100 such entries. The actual component produces 100 img elements; the JSON is 8,213 UTF-8 bytes, demonstrating there is no aggregate preview-count gate.

Separately stream 12,000 zero-valued 1-bit grayscale scanlines of 1,501 bytes each through zlib, count and discard compressed output. 18,012,000 filtered bytes compress to 17,525 bytes; with 57 bytes of normal PNG chunk/signature overhead this would be 17,582 bytes or 23,444 Base64 characters. This is far below the MCP 1,400,000-character and 2 MiB body caps, although a 12,000x12,000 RGBA raster is 576,000,000 bytes. No complete image was constructed or decoded.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared strict byte/signature/dimension validation before creating any media URL. Make image loading an explicit per-item action and bound simultaneous/aggregate preview resources, with useful rejection feedback and cleanup on release/owner changes. Preserve the original result receipt and raw JSON download path independently of preview eligibility.

findings.title: 旧实时会话的迟到回调会修改当前选中会话的语音与历史状态
findings.description: voiceStarted / voiceClosed 只比较传入 target 与闭包中的旧 threadId，没有核对 hook 当前选择、资源 epoch、API 或本次访问身份。hook 中的 voice、generation、controller 及 React state 则由后续选择继续复用。RealtimePanel 按 thread/epoch/lease 更换子组件后，旧组件仍可接收启动或停止结果；owned() 有意允许卸载后的清理，accept() 却也无条件调用旧 onStarted/onClosed，因而将清理结果传播到新会话状态。
confirmedEvidence: 本轮纯 hook 探针：保留 A 的 voiceClosed，切到 B 并令 B 语音活动，再调用旧 close(A)；B realtimeActive 从 true 变为 false，期望保持 true 的断言失败。此项只证明旧 callback 能污染共享 hook 状态，不作为真实双语音执行证明。

本轮组件探针使用真实 RealtimePanel、useConversation、useOperations 和 jsdom localStorage，仅 API 为本地替身。A 以文字实时方式启动，HTTP promise 未完成时切换 B；B 完整历史读取后 ready=true、realtimeActive=false。随后 A 启动返回 active，旧组件确实提交了 cleanup stop，但 B realtimeActive 变为 true，期望 false 的断言失败。探针没有启动 B 的实时会话，也没有使用 native、WebRTC、麦克风或网络。
reproduction: 在 A 会话发起实时会话启动，在其响应尚未完成时切换到 B。
让 B 的正常历史读取完成，再让旧 A 启动响应返回有效 active 状态。
旧面板 accept(result) 先执行保存的 onStarted(A)，之后才请求停止 A；此时 B 被错误标记为 realtimeActive 并失去历史 ready。
staticConsequences: invalidate() 会终止当前 B 的历史请求，清除 complete/ready，并将 B 标记为需要重新同步；普通输入因此会被阻止。
若旧 A 清理 stop 没有取得明确关闭响应，旧面板不再接收实时事件，B 的假活动标志可持续到当前会话主动重读。该持续分支为当前代码静态推导，未通过真实 native 集成验证。
旧 close 回调改变另一活动会话状态的 UI 可达性还受全局 pending 操作门控及回执到达顺序影响；本报告不将纯 hook 探针扩张为真实同时执行两条语音的证明。

The runtime requires an own answer for each question and therefore rejects this response; repeating the same UI action cannot answer the waiting native question.

findings.title: Separate Other selection state from literal answer values
findings.description: The UI uses the literal answer value __other as an internal Other-mode sentinel, and the submit loop applies that conversion to every question even when it has no options. Consequently a schema-valid literal __other option is shown as a custom-answer input even with isOther false; an options-null free-text question answered with the exact text __other is rejected locally as incomplete and never reaches onAnswer. These are legitimate protocol values and cannot be distinguished from mode state by comparing answer text.

findings.expected: Submit the exact selected or typed text; enable a separate Other mode only when offered by that question.
findings.actual: The offered literal opens an unoffered Other input; the free-text literal produces zero answer calls and cannot be submitted as entered.

evidence.detail: Option labels are strings and options may be null; both local fixtures passed the current official schema with isOther false.
A non-Other choice is valid when its text equals an offered label; free text has no label restriction.

tests: submits an officially valid literal __other option without opening an unoffered other answer
submits the literal __other as a free text answer with no select or custom-answer mode
evidence.actual: The option fixture rendered a custom input despite isOther false; the free-text fixture made zero onAnswer calls.

findings.recommendation: Track the selected option or Other mode separately from arbitrary user/option strings, and apply custom-answer substitution only to a question explicitly in Other mode. Cover both literal-option and free-text cases.

findings.trigger: Repeatedly create a paused automation and remove it. The create capacity check counts only non-removed rows; remove only changes state to removed. An isolated in-memory SQLite probe completed 1025 create/remove pairs and observed 1025 stored rows, all removed, with zero visible automations.
findings.impact: Deleted automation definitions grow without a retention bound and are scanned by subsequent list, due-collection, and capacity queries. The 1000-run recycling and receipt-generation rotation do not reclaim this table, so normal long-running create/delete usage bypasses the intended bounded persistent-resource model.
findings.recommendation: Delete or recycle removed definitions once no retained run needs them, or introduce a bounded tombstone retention policy. Preserve existing accepted operation receipts for idempotency; exercise repeated create/remove across the retention bound and receipt rotations.

findings.title: Late goal mutation responses overwrite newer goal notifications
findings.trigger: thread/goal/set returns an active goal after the runtime has processed a newer thread/goal/updated complete/paused notification, or thread/goal/clear returns after a newer active notification. NativeRpc can resolve a response and consume later notifications in the same stdout chunk before workflowMutation resumes.
findings.impact: The unconditional goalActive assignment resurrects a completed goal or hides a newer active goal. The reproduced completion case leaves runtime activity busy even when goal/get is complete, blocking direct work and idle-only maintenance/configuration until another goal mutation or runtime reload.
findings.recommendation: Version goal state at the final write boundary and apply response-derived goal/clear state only when no newer goal evidence has been consumed. Update continuation state versions when accepting mutation responses so concurrent continuation reads cannot overwrite them. Add deterministic tests for complete/paused/clear/active notifications and ordinary active goals.

findings.title: Late live-settings responses overwrite the actual rerouted model
findings.trigger: A turn/settings/update applied response resumes after a newer model/rerouted notification for the same active turn has installed a different toModel.
findings.impact: The older requested model overwrites activeModel and defeats subsequent input modality checks. The deterministic probe requests an audio-capable model, receives a reroute to a text-only model, then incorrectly dispatches an audio turn/steer.
findings.recommendation: Capture turn identity and relevant model/settings version at beforeWrite; accept response-derived model state only while those versions still match. findings.title: An older trust save clears a newer editable choice
findings.trigger: Select trusted and confirm, submit project/trust/write, hold its response, then change the still-enabled choice to untrusted. Resolve the original response successfully. The current choice becomes empty, although the only submitted write carried trusted. In Workspace, onChanged also changes the epoch used as the ProjectTrustSettings key, so accepting edits during the request can lose them through remounting as well.
findings.impact: The UI accepts and then silently discards a newer trust selection. The newer choice was not submitted, while the earlier trust change was applied. This is a small but reproducible form-state/data-entry regression; it does not itself send an unconfirmed second request.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the trust choice and its confirmation for the pending submission, including the period in which its result remains unknown. Alternatively retain a revision-owned draft across the onChanged/epoch remount; merely conditional setChoice clearing is insufficient for the real parent lifecycle. Add a deferred-response regression using the actual epoch/key relationship.

findings.title: Control rollback can remove the built-in-account downgrade guard
findings.trigger: After updating trusted control tools and activating built-in accounts or migrating HTTPS, invoke ordinary control-rollback for a committed generation whose capabilities provide system-v1/nativeWorkspace but predate built-in-account support.

findings.title: 在观察到 EOF 时启动独立的原生进程清理截止时间
findings.body: streaming 桥只在 input_ended 且 pending 已排空后设置 ended_at。若原生 CLI 持续存活但停止读取 stdin，桥内已积压的数据无法排空；即使已实际读到上游 EOF，ended_at 仍为 None，循环便永远到不了清理超时。NativeRpc.stop 的 launcher 分支仅 end stdin 并等待 6 秒，所以这一正常关闭路径会报告 cleanup unknown 并留下原生进程等待后续外部终止，而不是执行有界清理。
findings.trigger: 原生 CLI 不再读取 stdin，桥仍有待发数据，随后上游关闭输入。64 KiB 待发数据就能在尚未达到 8 MiB 输入容量的情况下实际观察 EOF 并触发此问题。
findings.impact: 依赖 EOF 的运行时关闭无法回收仍在运行的 CLI 及其后代，6 秒后进入 cleanup unknown；只有额外服务信号、原生进程自行退出或恢复读取才能解除。
findings.recommendation: EOF 一经观察就启动独立且不被排空逻辑延后的终止截止时间，允许在有限宽限期内排空数据，期满后进入已有 clean_children 流程。新增 CLI 不读取输入、已有待发字节且上游 EOF 的组合回归。

evidence.existingCoverageGap: tests/deploy/test_native_shutdown.py:62-64,85-86 的 EOF 场景没有先写输入；tests/deploy/test_deployment.py:735-747 的背压场景最终会读取输入。
evidence.reproductionKind: 从当前源码 AST 抽取 supervise，注入确定性的 selector、存活但不读取的子进程和时钟；最多 100 次轮询；不启动 OS 子进程或测试套件。
evidence.result: 空缓冲 EOF 在 2.1 秒进入清理并返回 0；64 KiB 待发字节在 0.2 秒已观察 EOF，10.1 秒后仍未自行清理，只有复现器限步异常才进入 finally。

findings.title: Release publication can commit before nested entries and final executable modes are durable
findings.trigger: A host power loss occurs after a newly exported nested release has been renamed, its manifest published and activation committed, but before the filesystem independently flushes unsynced nested directories or metadata changes.
findings.impact: snapshot fsyncs file data before chmod and only syncs the top export directory. Nested directory entries and the final executable modes have no guaranteed persistence. publish_release then syncs only the releases parent before publishing the durable manifest. A reboot can therefore leave a committed manifest/current pointer naming an incomplete or incorrectly permissioned release; integrity or process start fails and candidate recovery cannot rely on the previously verified tree.
findings.recommendation: Before publishing the release name or manifest, durably flush every copied regular file after its final metadata changes and every nested directory bottom-up, including parents containing symlinks. Use a shared no-follow durability helper consistent with control_update durable_tree. Preserve the rename/parent-sync/manifest ordering, and add a narrow ordering regression covering nested files and executable modes.
findings.evidence: Source inspection of the complete snapshot and publish_release paths; control_update already has an explicit bottom-up durable_tree operation for the analogous boundary. Parent reviewer independently confirmed the finding. No claim of physical power-failure reproduction.

findings.title: Persist each transaction directory name before starting lifecycle side effects
findings.trigger: On a Linux filesystem, power loss after a new lifecycle journal is written and services/pointers/definitions have changed, but before the transaction directory entry happens to reach durable storage.
findings.evidence: common.mkdir only creates/chmods/chowns a directory (common.py:75-80). write_json uses atomic_write, whose sole directory barrier is the immediate file parent (common.py:53-72). The release, provider, HTTPS, configuration-layer and uninstall paths create state/transactions/<id> and flush state.json inside it, but never fsync state/transactions before side effects or their terminal record. Consequently the retained journal can disappear while durable pointer/config/unit changes survive. The strongest complete chain is uninstall_services: mkdir journal.parent (209), write journal (212), publish config/uninstalled.json referring to its ID (213-214), stop/remove units and sudo entry (220-228), terminal journal and durable uninstalled marker (234-236). restore_services then requires that missing journal and its before image. Ordinary pending transaction discovery can also miss a lost release/provider/config/HTTPS transaction.

affectedLocations.behavior: release prepared journal precedes stop; no transactions-parent barrier through committed write at408
provider prepared journal precedes stop/select; no transactions-parent barrier through committed write at458
configuration-layer journal precedes barriers and stop; no transactions-parent barrier through committed write at302
uninstall marker refers to an unflushed transaction-directory name before definitions are durably removed
same collection publication defect for input/cache/prepared build evidence through prepared.json at345; release tree and manifest themselves have separate correct barriers

findings.impact: Recovery material and transaction discovery are not crash-durable. A successful uninstall can retain an uninstalled marker while losing the only saved definitions required by restore-services; interrupted mutations can become undiscoverable.
findings.recommendation: Use a shared durable directory publication operation that verifies trusted ancestry and flushes the directory plus its parent chain, including existing directories on interrupted retry. Require it before the first dependent side effect. Add fault-injection assertions that a failed parent barrier prevents stop, pointer/config selection and uninstall deletion.
findings.verification: Fresh full source reads and caller/terminal-write tracing. No power-cut simulation or live service execution was performed.

findings.title: Make the root management receipt directory durable before dispatching a mutation
findings.trigger: The first root management mutation creates state/receipts, reaches the requested side effect, and the machine loses power before the new receipts directory entry is durably published in state.
findings.evidence: dispatch creates receipts at625 and atomically writes running at626, then dispatches restart/provider changes and writes completed at666. Both write_json calls only fsync receipts, not state. Installation build_plan does not precreate receipts (install_recovery.py:304-313). There is no later fsync(state) in this dispatch chain. preflight_mutation regards an absent receipt as new at manager.py:583-609; operation/read reports not_received for an absent file at655.
findings.impact: A management action may finish but its durable idempotency record can disappear. Later root reconciliation returns not_received and a repeated original request can execute again, violating the manager receipt contract.
findings.recommendation: Durably publish the receipts directory and relevant ancestors before the initial running receipt and before entering any action. Preserve replay behavior when the directory already exists after an interrupted attempt; test parent fsync failure prevents invocation.
findings.verification: Fresh semantic read of initialization, mutation preflight, dispatch, receipt lookup and atomic write implementation. This concerns the root manager receipt layer, not a claim that gateway SQLite receipts lack their own persistence.

findings.title: Flush publication-directory ancestry before acknowledging retained generations and initial installation
findings.trigger: Power loss after selecting a newly staged certificate/CA, saving the first provider profile, or completing an installation whose managed top-level containers were newly created.
findings.evidence: stage_tls creates config/tls/<revision> and atomic-writes the files (333-341); stage_tls_ca does the same under tls-ca (376-383). Those writes flush only the revision directory. setup_https later durably writes Caddyfile, instance.json and https.json and commits (565-605), but never flushes tls or tls-ca, so the selected revision name can be lost. Profiles.save creates config/provider-profiles then writes the profile (provider_lifecycle.py:79-83); the save-only provider action returns immediately (manager.py:419-426) and never flushes config, so the first saved collection can disappear. initialize_recorded precreates app.parent/state.parent/control.parent (install_recovery.py:391-393) without flushing their parents, while root_lock creates config.parent (37) without flushing its parent before the initialization record is relied upon. CreationPlan publishes children and flushes their immediate parents (294), which does not persist the precreated container names in /opt, /var/lib or /usr/lib. Existing-plan entries return after verify (250-253), so retry also cannot be used as a guaranteed missing publication barrier.

affectedLocations.behavior: initial configuration-container ancestry and initial recovery record
new installation containers acknowledged after only descendant publication
existing verified entries skip a publication barrier during retry

findings.impact: A successfully selected TLS revision can be absent at reboot and prevent Caddy/HTTPS health startup; an acknowledged saved profile or a newly created installation container can disappear despite its files having been flushed.
findings.recommendation: Centralize trusted durable directory creation/publication, flush every newly created ancestor and re-establish missing barriers on retry before references or successful results are exposed. Keep initial lock creation ownership/symlink validation intact. Exercise TLS/CA and first-profile ordering plus initial container/retry paths with injected fsync failures.
findings.verification: Fresh full semantic reads, traced all generation publishers. ProviderStore.select explicitly flushes providers at provider.py:286, control update explicitly flushes record/barrier parents and transaction collection, request staging flushes its collection, workspace helpers use descriptor-relative parent barriers, and publish_release flushes releases and app. Those paths were not mislabeled as equivalent committed-generation failures. No physical crash test was performed.

Add interaction regressions for queue text and goal objective/budget surviving tab round trips, pending/rejected edit round trips and owner changes.

These affect the shared primary action style, including save configuration and publish-sharing confirmation, rather than only decorative text or disabled controls.

findings.title: Make native integration fixture teardown survive startup and cleanup failures
findings.description: The guardian fixture starts a referenced loopback HTTP server before catalog/config writes and RuntimeService.create, but it only exposes close() after those operations succeed. If a write or native startup rejects, the caller has not yet entered its try/finally and the listener has no remaining cleanup path. The returned close() also awaits service.close() before closing the server, so an intentionally propagated native cleanup failure skips server cleanup. The PTY test similarly writes diagnostic output before calling f.close() in finally; a failed diagnostic write skips all teardown. These are concrete failure paths that leave test listeners or owned process trees active and can prevent clean test-worker exit; they are not a claimed production runtime defect.

findings.title: Recheck live owner before project registration after asynchronous resolution
findings.description: project/add checks requireConnection at admission, then awaits project/resolve and commits ledger.addProject without checking that the same authenticated browser owner is still live. controlFlow: GatewayServer captures the exact browser connection and supplies a callback that rechecks session/CSRF, WebSocket identity and OPEN/connecting/disconnecting state (server.ts266-271).

Dispatcher invokes that callback before the asynchronous resolver (dispatch.ts119), but its local beforeWrite only marks the receipt dispatching (132); the post-resolver addProject at144 has no callback.

Gateway revocation closes the browser socket; eventual close cleanup sends worker /disconnect. Runtime beforeWrite fences the current worker-channel/client lease, but it cannot undo or authorize a subsequent gateway-local commit after the read-only resolver result returns.

Automation commands and rotation already recheck after their await boundaries (dispatch.ts190 and64). Synchronous project/remove and operation/retire have no analogous await gap. Worktree/receipt reconciliation after a successful backend execution records existing positive evidence and should not be rolled back on disconnect.

reproduction.limits: In-memory Dispatcher and controlled worker only; no native worker, network, paid model, test runner, or real project filesystem.

findings.title: Revalidate browser authorization before a queued mutation is written

GatewayServer's captured requireConnection does check auth.require immediately and would reject the revoked account; however it is not called at this boundary. Revocation closes the browser WebSocket, while worker /disconnect cleanup follows the asynchronous socket close event, leaving a window for a queued mutation to dispatch and receive a durable accepted receipt after revocation. This finding concerns work not yet sent at revocation; replaying a previously accepted receipt remains intentionally permitted after ordinary browser lease loss.

findings.title: Recycle acknowledged browser receipt markers without reviving stale operations
findings.trigger: Ordinary completed mutations accumulate one permanent harness.acknowledged.v1.<UUID>=1 localStorage key apiece (most non-input writes acknowledge automatically). The 200-record guard excludes these keys. Continued use of the same origin eventually fills its localStorage quota, even when previous operations were all handled; any existing origin data reduces headroom.
findings.observed: Actual current-source reproduction with a 65536-byte synthetic quota completed 531 accepted/acknowledged operations, retaining 531 markers (64782 bytes). Operation 532 became accepted but acknowledgement failed with QuotaExceededError. Re-query/reconcile of that original accepted receipt succeeded; acknowledgement and creation of an unrelated operation still failed with QuotaExceededError. The UI catches and displays the storage exception; no silent dispatch or automatic replay was observed.
findings.scale: Each generated UUID marker uses 122 UTF-16 bytes in the fixture accounting. A hypothetical 5 MiB allowance corresponds to roughly 42974 markers before overhead or other entries; this is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measured browser quota or a claim of near-term failure.
findings.impact: Persistent loss of new mutation capability for a long-lived browser origin, with no product-supported local marker compaction/recovery. Handling the remaining accepted record cannot release capacity because acknowledgement must first add another key. Server receipt generation maintenance does not remove browser markers. Clearing origin data manually can discard unrelated pending/unknown recovery identities and is not an adequate safe recovery flow.
findings.requirements: OP-05 requires visible fail-closed storage errors and includes reaching capacity, handling a record and retrying. The current path satisfies visible fail-closed behavior but has no capacity recovery for handled markers. OP-04 also requires late observations never undo an acknowledged fact; existing markers fulfill that invariant and must not simply be deleted.
findings.recommendation: Provide a bounded local retention/maintenance design with a persistent generation floor or equivalent cross-tab coordination that safely retires handled markers. Preserve pending/unknown identities and suppress late writes from old tabs across compaction/reload. Offer observable local capacity status and a safe maintenance path; do not use naked TTL/removal of acknowledged keys.

findings.title: Accepted receipt clears newer memory-only draft after persistence failure
findings.description: While submitted draft A awaits its HTTP response, the editable composer accepts newer input B. If persisting B fails, useDraft keeps B in memory and explicitly tells the user the input remains in the page. The accepted A receipt clears the stored revision A and emits a key-only harness-drafts event. The matching hook unconditionally reloads storage, replacing B with an empty draft and clearing the save-failure warning. B was never sent and has no persistent copy, so this is actual user-input loss.
findings.trigger: Persist A; dispatch turn/start through real Api.beginMutation and hold its synthetic HTTP response; type B while persistence fails; release an accepted response for A. findings.observed: Normal-persistence control retains B. Both injected QuotaExceededError and the unmocked application capacity rejection show B visible before acknowledgement and A still in storage; after acceptance, visible text is empty, the draft storage key is absent, the warning is empty, and the durable operation is accepted. Each scenario dispatches exactly one synthetic request containing A only.

findings.title: Model catalog consumers drop pagination, making later models and reasoning choices unreachable

AutomationsPanel forwards only models.items, and AutomationForm renders these options without a cursor/loading/error/refresh or more-model control. ConfigSettings owns a separate 50-row usePaged but never exposes models.more, models.hasMore or model errors; a configured model on a later page has no available reasoning choices, and its configuration refresh button does not refresh this catalog. The native-provider ModelCatalog branch separately requests limit:100 with useResource and ignores nextCursor; discovery simply refreshes the first page, silently omitting model 101 onward. findings.title: Recorded service restoration rejects its exact retained legacy sudo policy and leaves services stopped
findings.trigger: An existing instance has the recognized pre-registry sudo policy without catalog-server. control-update retains that policy, then candidate-archive performs recorded uninstall/restore; the same issue affects a direct recorded uninstall/restore.
findings.evidence: Ownership now correctly accepts the exact legacy policy. restore_services publishes the recorded before.sudo bytes, restores activity, then calls ordinary Manager.verify. That verifier permits only sudo_rule() (and current workspace=False where applicable), both containing catalog-server; it rejects the retained old bytes. The restore exception path reinstalls barriers, stops all roles, and leaves the lifecycle journal pending. Candidate archival can already have moved the verified candidate before this failure.
findings.impact: A legitimate maintenance restore leaves the instance stopped and pending. Configuration-layer migration, which would install the new policy, is blocked by that pending lifecycle transaction; repeating restore reproduces the failure.
findings.requiredFix: Keep ordinary final verification strict. Permit the exact legacy catalog policy only when restoring a protected, identity-bound lifecycle snapshot that contains those exact bytes, retain root ownership/mode/link/content checks and every other integrity check, and add restore/archive regressions that call real Manager.verify plus altered-policy failure/pending-state coverage.
findings.confirmation: Independently confirmed by v220-final-runtime and root. No archive or service stop was executed on the online instance.
